correctness.rationale: With explicit LCF and bipartite adjacency, two standalone and independently structured programs exhaust all 495 four-sets, 792 five-sets and all admissible one-vertex replacements of the 324 minimum sets. Parallel bitmask and serial force processing both give no successful four-set, 324 successful five-sets, token-jump and token-slide edges of 2910 and 534 respectively, connectivity, radii 5 and 9 and diameters 5 and 13. Full all-pairs shortest paths show the sharp distance-nine slide detour for some jump-adjacent pair and no larger such detour. A separate standard-library automorphism backtracking program finds 48 automorphisms and 9 orbits with consistent representative eccentricities. The programs were executed from the packaged paths; all three stored output files match. Exhaustive finite computation is a proof here because it precisely covers all candidate sets and moves; there is no inference to an infinite family.

originality.rationale: The 2010 foundational arXiv paper provides ordinary forcing background. The full relevant sections of the 2020 Geneson–Haas–Hogben preprint define the jump exchange graph and analyze families such as forests, paths and constructed examples rather than a Franklin graph census. The 2025 Bong et al. preprint treats PSD/skew forcing primarily, and its general data sets do not specialize to these 12-vertex exact values. MathWorld identifies the Franklin, crossed-prism and Knödel aliases but does not give this forcing configuration geometry. Published mathematical-record hits on Franklin graphs concern paired domination and matching-complex topology; none implies the 324-set census, two diameters or maximum nine-slide direct-jump distortion. Targeted source and parameter searches found no covering implication, with residual uncertainty for unindexed work.

value.rationale: This classifies an entire optimum-sensor-placement space on the canonical Franklin graph, including its nine graph-automorphism orbits and two natural move geometries. It exhibits both global local-move connectivity and a large quantitative penalty (diameter 13 versus 5), with a sharp nine-slide shortest reconfiguration needed even for a single unrestricted swap. The directly motivated invariant distinguishes local relocation feasibility from unconstrained substitution; it is not just the already studied optimum cardinality. It is finite and not advertised as a general graph-family theorem.
